newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-CLARKE LEADER BY TWO, WOODS FALLS AWAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CLARKE LEADER BY TWO, WOODS FALLS AWAY.

text.p: Briton Darren Clarke sank five 20-foot birdie putts in a five-under-par 66 to earn a two-stroke lead over American Justin Leonard at the halfway mark in the British Open on Friday.
Swede Jesper Parnevik, runner-up in the 1994 Open at Turnberry, was one shot behind Leonard, both men also shooting 66 on a sunny, relatively calm day at Royal Troon.
Masters champion Tiger Woods was 13 shots off the lead after a three-over-par 74 that included a quadruple bogey eight at the 10th hole, where he lost a battle with a gorse bush.
Fred Couples shared fourth spot a shot behind Parnevik after a 68 that surprised him as he has not played much and cannot practice because of his bad back.
Couples was level with English qualifier David Tapping, who also shot a 66 in this, his first British Open.
American Jim Furyk, who shared the first round lead with Clarke, slipped to a 72 and now shares sixth spot with U.S. Ryder Cup captain Tom Kite, round in 67.
Clarke's 67-66 start equalled the record for the first 36 holes in Opens at Royal Troon set by American Bobby Clampett in 1982.

Most of the big names survived the halfway cut which was made at 147 -- five over. The biggest casualties were 1994 champion Nick Price of Zimbabwe and three times winner Seve Ballesteros, who missed out for 11th time in 13 events this year despite a level-par 71.
Clarke, third in the European Ryder Cup standings, blazed the front nine with six birdies, two bogeys and just one par.
"I got my momentum early and just kept going," said the burly player from Dungannon in Northern Ireland.
He admitted he was beginning to think about the possibility of winning after saying on Thursday he regarded just getting close as the next step in his career.
"If I can get myself into contention on Sunday afternoon, I do believe I can give it a go," he said.
Leonard's round was highlighted by eagles at the downwind fourth and sixth holes as the former U.S. amateur champion hit both greens with five-iron second shots and holed from 15 and 20 feet.
He had four birdies and three bogeys, one at the last where he three-putted.

"I don't know if I'm that surprised. I'm very pleased but I have been playing well," said Leonard, who won the Kemper Open last month and finished fifth and third in his last two events before coming here.

Parnevik, who changed to a new putter after his first round 70 because he did not feel comfortable on the greens, used the new club to good effect with an eagle three at the fourth and a 50 foot putt to save par at the last.

Woods was level for the day on the front nine but sent his drive on the 10th into the rough. He then fired an eight-iron into thick gorse and an attempted sand wedge caught the bush on his downswing and he barely moved the ball. He hacked his fourth just six yards, chipped past the green with his fifth, chipped up to 12 feet and two-putted.
The eight followed a triple-bogey seven at the 11th hole in his first round 72.
"If you take away those two holes I could be three-under. Other than that I've hit the ball very well this week," said Woods, who made the cut by two shots.

Defending champion Tom Lehman was level with Woods after a 72 in which he took a triple-bogey seven at the second which included a two-shot penalty for not replacing his marker in the correct place on the green.
Lehman moved his marker out of the line of a playing partner's putt and forgot to move it back when his turn came.

U.S. Open champion Ernie Els shot a two-under 69 to get back to two-over while three times champion Nick Faldo carded a 73 to be plus two. Colin Montgomerie survived the cut for only the second time in six years with a 69.
There were holes-in-one from Swedes Dennis Edlund at the Postage Stamp eighth and Daniel Olsson at the fifth.
